content: Antihistamines are medications that work by blocking histamine receptors in the body. Histamine is a chemical involved in allergic reactions and is also associated with symptoms such as a runny nose, sneezing, and watery eyes. When used for the common cold, antihistamines may help alleviate some of these symptoms, particularly those related to nasal congestion and excessive mucus production. However, their effectiveness in treating the common cold is limited, as the cold is caused by viral infections, and antihistamines do not directly target the underlying virus. Some antihistamines, especially first-generation ones, may also cause drowsiness as a side effect, which can sometimes be beneficial for individuals experiencing difficulty sleeping due to cold symptoms.
